concepts.learning_objective: Explain why India's leaders chose the democratic path and how they viewed the purpose of politics.
Describe how the Election Commission prepared for the first general election, including delimitation and electoral rolls.

topics.title: The first general election and changing methods of voting
topics.ncert_sections: Challenge of building democracy; Changing methods of voting

concepts.learning_objective: Evaluate why the 1952 general election was a landmark in the history of democracy.
Trace the change from candidate-wise ballot boxes to stamped ballot papers and the EVM.

topics.title: Congress dominance in the first three general elections
topics.ncert_sections: Congress dominance in the first three general elections; Communist victory in Kerala

concepts.learning_objective: Recall the extent of Congress victories in the 1952, 1957 and 1962 elections.
Analyse how the first-past-the-post system magnified the Congress's seat share.
Describe the Communist victory in Kerala in 1957 and its dismissal in 1959.
Distinguish the Congress's dominance under democratic conditions from one-party rule elsewhere.
Explain the factors rooted in the freedom struggle that led to Congress dominance.

topics.title: Congress as social and ideological coalition; tolerance and management of factions
topics.ncert_sections: Congress as social and ideological coalition; Tolerance and management of factions

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how the Congress became a broad social and ideological coalition.
Analyse how factionalism worked within the Congress and why the period is called the 'Congress system'.

topics.title: Emergence of opposition parties
topics.ncert_sections: Emergence of opposition parties; Socialist Party; Communist Party of India; Bharatiya Jana Sangh

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the leaders, ideologies and positions of the Socialist Party, the CPI and the Bharatiya Jana Sangh.
Evaluate the role opposition parties played in keeping the system democratic despite few seats.
